candidates.buyer: Licensed bars, retail bottle stores, clubs, nightclubs and restaurants
candidates.evidence: https://wikiprocedure.com/index.php/Tonga_-_Obtain_Liquor_Licence ; https://paclii.org/to/legis/num_act/ila2010320 ; https://matangitonga.to/print/6485 (seven licence categories, Police Commissioner chairs the Liquor Licensing Authority)
candidates.existing: None seen. The authority is run from Tonga Police headquarters, with no online system found.
candidates.name: Liquor licence renewal and compliance pack (bars, bottle stores, clubs, restaurants)
candidates.trigger: Liquor Licensing Act amended 2010. Renewal is due 30 days before expiry and needs a tax clearance, Ministry of Works suitability permit, fire safety report, police clearance, health inspection report and a host responsibility policy. A late fee applies. Procedure details are from a third-party wiki and may be out of date.
candidates.unchecked: Number of licensees, current fees and categories, whether renewal is online, and the competitor search (not run, budget used up).

candidates.buyer: Sole traders, family firms and small companies that hold a Tongan business licence
candidates.category: 33. Business licence annual renewal and registry filings
candidates.evidence: https://businessregistries.gov.to/?p=250 ; https://businessregistries.gov.to/Documentation/TO/How to obtain a business licence.pdf ; https://wikiprocedure.com/index.php/Tonga_-_Reinstate_Business_Licence ; https://pacliirms.paclii.org/to/legis/sub_leg/rsaa2002rsar2015885.pdf (tax clearance)
candidates.existing: The government's online registry already handles filing and sends a reminder email. Local accounting firms probably do it by hand.
candidates.name: Business licence and tax clearance renewal reminder and filing service for quiet SMEs
candidates.trigger: Business Licences Act 2002: yearly online 'notice of continued business activity'. The licence is cancelled after a 3-month grace period and reinstated for T$100 (third-party wiki) plus penalties. Companies must file an annual return, with a late fee after one month and removal after six months. Tax clearance is required for business or liquor licences.
candidates.unchecked: A 2013 press report said licences would become permanent, which conflicts with the registry guide; competitor search not run; whether filing is simple enough that no service is needed.

candidates.buyer: Licensed fish processing establishments, seaweed exporters, aquarium fish exporters and fishers feeding HACCP-certified outlets
candidates.category: 34. Fisheries processing, seaweed and aquarium export licences
candidates.existing: None seen. This was not a direct search.
candidates.name: Fish export HACCP and licence records pack for small processors, fish markets and seaweed exporters
candidates.trigger: Fisheries Management (Processing and Export) Regulations 2008: HACCP plan, export licence, export log sheets, health certificate and inspections. Aquaculture Management Regulations 2020/2022 need an export permit and a HACCP plan. A June 2026 report says the Tu'imatamoana Fish Market was certified for export under HACCP, with training for fishermen.
candidates.unchecked: Number of licensed establishments (probably a handful), whether the Ministry sets electronic record formats, the competent authority for seafood safety, and the competitor search.

candidates.buyer: Small guest houses, backpackers, beach fales and home stays, many of them family-run
candidates.category: 29. Hotels, guest houses and short-term rentals
candidates.name: Tourism accommodation registration pack for guest houses, beach fales and home stays
candidates.trigger: Tonga Tourism Authority Act 2012 defines accommodation to include these. The registration, licensing and levy duties are not confirmed. The business licence form also lists tourism-related activities for extra approval.
candidates.unchecked: The Act's registration section, any guest register or levy, how many operators, and any competitor.

candidates.buyer: About 20 licensed whale-swim operators (Vava'u, Ha'apai and Tongatapu)
candidates.category: 32. Whale watching and swimming operator licences
candidates.name: Whale watching and swimming operator licence and season compliance
candidates.trigger: Whale Watching and Swimming Act 2008 and Regulations 2013: licence applications to the Minister of Tourism, licence number cap (20 in the 2020 gazette notice), season 1 July to 30 November. Licence validity is unclear: 2 years, 3 years or annual. A 2025 Court of Appeal case by Vava'u licence holders is pending or unknown.
candidates.unchecked: Too few buyers on the evidence; reporting duties not checked.

candidates.buyer: Importers and dealers of used vehicles (plus individual importers)
candidates.category: 35. Vehicle import age ban and customs orders
candidates.existing: ASYCUDA World already handles customs entries (K04).
candidates.name: Used vehicle importer and dealer pack for the 10-year import age ban
candidates.trigger: A ban on importing vehicles aged 10 years or older was reinstated 22 Nov 2024, deferred on 21 Feb 2025, and postponed again to 30 June 2026 by Cabinet on 13 Feb 2026. It is a one-off deadline, and I did not check what happened after 30 June 2026.
candidates.unchecked: Current status of the ban, whether the importer count is meaningful, and whether any recurring record duty follows.

candidates.buyer: Registered co-operatives, incorporated societies and charitable trusts, many of them church or community bodies
candidates.name: Co-operative and incorporated society (including church) annual return service
candidates.trigger: Co-operative Societies Act Cap 118 (Registrar, audit and inspection) and Incorporated Societies Act Cap 28. Annual filing duties and deadlines are unconfirmed.
candidates.unchecked: Whether returns are required and enforced, the number of bodies, and the responsible registrar.

candidates.buyer: Licensed pharmacies, medicine importers and wholesalers
candidates.name: Pharmacy premises and therapeutic goods licence tracker
candidates.trigger: Pharmacy Act 2001 (premises licence, Form 3), Pharmacy Regulations 2010, and Therapeutic Goods Regulations 2011 (separate licences for import, wholesale, retail supply and manufacture, with a fee for each).
candidates.unchecked: The number of licensees is likely very small, and renewal cycles and 2024-26 amendments were not checked.

candidates.buyer: NRBT-authorised money transfer and foreign exchange providers (about 18 persons, plus sub-agents)
candidates.category: 19. Market traders, street vendors, money changers
candidates.known_note: Same buyer group and duty as K02; no re-check done.
candidates.name: Pacific MTO AML compliance kit (Tonga module)
candidates.trigger: Foreign Exchange Control Act 2018 s13 licensing by the NRBT Non-Banks Unit. AML/CFT guideline 2015. Enforcement example: NRBT action against LWS Trading and RK3 Pacific in May 2024.

candidates.category: 30. Small exporters and importers facing traceability or certification rules
candidates.known_note: Same group and duty as K01; K05 covers the government quarantine system.
candidates.name: Kava and plant export permit and phytosanitary paperwork
candidates.trigger: MAFFF Quarantine export permit per consignment, phytosanitary certificate, accreditation code and exporter registration.

candidates.buyer: Private lessors and lessees of registered leases (landlords of town and tax allotments)
candidates.category: 36. Land leases and tax allotment rent
candidates.name: Land lease rent arrears and renewal tracker for private lessors of tax allotments
candidates.trigger: Land Act lease form: arrears, lessor's lien, forfeiture, and Cabinet rent reviews.
candidates.unchecked: It is not an authority-imposed recurring duty, so it may be out of scope; no 2024-26 rule found.

coverage.category: 1. Household employers: domestic workers, live-in carers, nannies
coverage.found: No dedicated search; no sign of a registration duty for household employers. Budget.

coverage.category: 2. Scrap-metal dealers
coverage.found: Waste Management Act 2005 has a registration and licensing section (Part VIII) but I found no scrap-specific licence. Waste Authority Limited is the approved authority on Tongatapu. Nothing found.

coverage.category: 3. Second-hand dealers and pawnbrokers
coverage.found: Budget; not searched.

coverage.category: 4. Gold and jewellery buyers
coverage.found: Only that dealers in precious metals are covered by the 2015 NRBT AML/CFT guideline (covered-entity list). No current rule found.

coverage.category: 5. Used car parts and vehicle dismantlers
coverage.found: No dismantler rules found. Related: the ban on importing vehicles aged 10 years or older, postponed to 30 June 2026 (see candidate).

coverage.category: 6. Livestock traders, markets and animal transport
coverage.found: Budget; not searched.

coverage.category: 7. Small abattoirs and butchers
coverage.found: Budget; not searched.

coverage.category: 8. Beekeepers
coverage.found: Budget; not searched. Likely negligible.

coverage.category: 9. Veterinary practices and veterinary medicine sellers
coverage.found: Budget; not searched.

coverage.category: 10. Well drillers and water abstraction
coverage.found: Budget; not searched.

coverage.category: 11. Septic, sanitation and waste haulers
coverage.found: Waste Management Act 2005 only; Waste Authority Limited runs Tongatapu service. No hauler licence detail found.

coverage.category: 12. Lift, boiler and pressure-equipment owners and inspectors
coverage.found: Budget; not searched.

coverage.category: 13. Small water systems
coverage.found: Budget; not searched.

coverage.category: 14. Pesticide and fertiliser dealers and applicators
coverage.found: Budget; not searched. Application form lists 'agricultural products' as needing extra approval, with no detail.

coverage.category: 15. Labour contractors and recruitment agencies
coverage.found: Tonga's labour sending unit is the government's Overseas Employment Division (Ministry of Internal Affairs). I found no private recruiter licence regime in Tonga. Buyers on the PALM scheme are Australian employers, outside Tonga.

coverage.category: 16. Cemeteries, burial societies and funeral services
coverage.found: Budget; not searched.

coverage.category: 17. Community and religious bodies
coverage.found: Incorporated Societies Act (Cap 28) exists, plus a Charitable Trusts regime. I could not confirm annual filing duties or a deadline. Search returned mostly NZ results for Tongan churches.

coverage.category: 18. Transport operators: minibus, taxi, moto-taxi, small trucking and bus fleets
coverage.found: Traffic Act 2020 covers vehicle and driver licensing, run by the Ministry of Infrastructure Land Transport Division. The business licence form lists taxi services as needing extra approval. I found no passenger permit rules or a Land Transport Act 2024.

coverage.category: 19. Market traders, street vendors, money changers
coverage.found: Foreign exchange and money transfer business needs a licence under Foreign Exchange Control Act 2018 s13, from the NRBT Non-Banks Unit. About 18 authorised persons in Types A, B and C. Hawking local produce is outside the Business Licences Act. Money transfer is covered by K02.

coverage.category: 20. Small licensed premises with inspections
coverage.found: Not searched specifically. Liquor premises were screened under category 31.

coverage.category: 21. Fuel stations and fuel or LPG distributors
coverage.found: Budget. The application form lists flammable goods and gas services as extra-approval activities, with no detail.

coverage.category: 22. Grain, coffee, cocoa and other commodity traders, millers and warehouses
coverage.found: No such commodity trade in Tonga. Kava and root-crop exports are under category 30 and K01.

coverage.category: 23. Co-operatives, credit unions and savings groups
coverage.found: Co-operative Societies Act (Cap 118) has a Registrar and audit and inspection provisions. I could not find return deadlines, the number of societies or the responsible ministry. Likely tiny.

coverage.category: 24. Private clinics, labs and other health providers that bill insurers or state schemes
coverage.found: Budget. No insurer-billing market is evident.

coverage.category: 25. Pharmacies, medicine importers, controlled chemicals
coverage.found: Pharmacy Act 2001, Pharmacy Regulations 2010 and Therapeutic Goods Act 2001 with Regulations 2011. Licences are needed for pharmacy premises and for importing, wholesale, retail and manufacturing of medicines. Ministry of Health administers them. Very few licensees.

coverage.category: 26. Security, cleaning and manpower agencies
coverage.found: Budget; not searched.

coverage.category: 27. Construction, mining and quarry contractors and suppliers
coverage.found: Budget. The application form lists electrical and construction services as extra-approval activities, with no detail.

coverage.category: 28. Notaries, land agents, real estate brokers, AML professionals
coverage.found: The 2015 NRBT AML/CFT guideline covers lawyers, accountants, real estate agents, precious-metals dealers, casinos and trust and company service providers. I found no 2024-26 update. Small buyer universe.

coverage.category: 29. Hotels, guest houses and short-term rentals
coverage.found: Tonga Tourism Authority Act 2012 defines accommodation to include guest houses, beach fales, backpackers and home stays. I could not read registration or licensing duties or any guest register rule. Unverified.

coverage.category: 30. Small exporters and importers facing traceability or certification rules
coverage.found: Kava and plant exports: MAFFF Quarantine export permit per consignment, phytosanitary certificate, accreditation code, exporter registration (Trade Portal). Fish exports: Fisheries Management (Processing and Export) Regulations 2008 require a licensed HACCP establishment, a health certificate and export log sheets. Nothing new beyond K01 and K05 for kava and quarantine.

coverage.category: 31. Liquor licensing (Liquor Licensing Authority, Tonga Police)
coverage.found: Seven licence categories. Renewal is due 30 days before expiry and needs a tax clearance, fire safety report, health inspection report, police clearance and a host responsibility policy. See candidate.

coverage.category: 32. Whale watching and swimming operator licences (Ministry of Tourism)
coverage.found: Whale Watching and Swimming Act 2008 and Regulations 2013. Licences are capped at about 20 and the season runs 1 July to 30 November. Tiny buyer group. See candidate.

coverage.category: 33. Business licence annual renewal and registry filings (Business Licences Act 2002, Companies annual returns)
coverage.found: Business licence is renewed yearly by an online 'notice of continued business activity'. It is cancelled after a 3-month grace period and reinstated for T$100 plus penalties. Companies file an annual return with late fees. A tax clearance form is needed for licences and for transfers overseas. See candidate.

coverage.category: 34. Fisheries processing, seaweed and aquarium export licences (Ministry of Fisheries)
coverage.found: Fisheries guide lists processing establishment licence T$550 and seaweed processing/export licence T$1,020, plus fishing vessel registration and licences at T$5 for vessels up to 6 m. A June 2026 report says the Tu'imatamoana Fish Market was certified for HACCP export. See candidate.

coverage.category: 35. Vehicle import age ban and customs orders (Ministry of Revenue and Customs)
coverage.found: Ban on importing vehicles 10 years or older was reinstated 22 Nov 2024, deferred 21 Feb 2025, and postponed again to 30 June 2026 (Cabinet, 13 Feb 2026). I did not check what happened after 30 June 2026.

coverage.category: 36. Land leases and tax allotment rent (Ministry of Lands, Land Act)
coverage.found: Court cases show recurring rent arrears, liens and forfeiture, and Cabinet rent reviews. I found no online system or 2024-26 rule change.

coverage.category: 37. Employer social security and PAYE (National Retirement Benefits Fund, MORC)
coverage.found: Employers must register with MORC for PAYE and with the retirement fund. Contributions are monthly and there is an annual reconciliation (reportedly 31 Aug, unverified). Rates conflict between third-party sources. This is general payroll, so out of scope.
